CAP_OVERFLOW.title: Over capacity
CAP_OVERFLOW.why: Work above the line does not disappear — it lands late, or it pushes something else out. Deciding which is the point of planning.
CAP_NEAR_LIMIT.title: Nearly full
CAP_NEAR_LIMIT.message: {team} is at {utilisation}% in {quarterId}, with {headroom} units left.
CAP_NEAR_LIMIT.explanation: The quarter is close enough to full that one more commitment tips it over.
CAP_NEAR_LIMIT.why: A quarter with no headroom absorbs nothing unexpected, and something unexpected always arrives.
CAP_NO_DELIVERABLE.title: No deliverable capacity
CAP_NO_DELIVERABLE.message: {team} has no deliverable capacity in {quarterId}, but work is placed there.
CAP_NO_DELIVERABLE.explanation: Reserves of {reserved} take the whole {effectiveCapacity}-unit container.
CAP_NO_DELIVERABLE.why: Every unit placed here is over by definition. Either the reserves are wrong or the work cannot happen.
CAP_PRIMARY_FOOTPRINT_MISSING.title: No primary placement
CAP_PRIMARY_FOOTPRINT_MISSING.message: {commitment} is owned by {primaryTeam} but has no placement there.
CAP_PRIMARY_FOOTPRINT_MISSING.explanatio: Committed work carries exactly one primary footprint, on the team that owns it.
CAP_PRIMARY_FOOTPRINT_MISSING.why: Without it, nobody is accountable for the work and no team-quarter is counting its cost.
CAP_NO_FOOTPRINT.title: Committed but not placed
CAP_NO_FOOTPRINT.message: {commitment} is {lifecycle} with nothing placed on the board.
CAP_NO_FOOTPRINT.explanation: Committed work consumes capacity somewhere. This consumes none.
CAP_NO_FOOTPRINT.why: Work nobody has made room for is work that will displace something else without warning.
CAP_SPAN_LONG.title: Spans many quarters
CAP_SPAN_LONG.explanation: Long-running work is harder to size, harder to review, and harder to stop.
CAP_SPAN_LONG.why: Splitting it into pieces that each finish gives you somewhere to change your mind.
CAP_ADJUSTMENT_UNEXPLAINED.title: Unexplained capacity change
CAP_ADJUSTMENT_UNEXPLAINED.message: {team} in {quarterId} is adjusted by {adjustment} units with no note.
CAP_ADJUSTMENT_UNEXPLAINED.explanation: The container is a different size from the team default, and nothing says why.
CAP_ADJUSTMENT_UNEXPLAINED.why: An overload with a visible symptom and no visible cause is the hardest kind to argue about.
DEP_OVERDUE.title: Dependency overdue
DEP_OVERDUE.why: Overdue prerequisites are the most common cause of a missed target quarter.
DEP_DUE_SOON.title: Dependency due soon
DEP_DUE_SOON.why: A prerequisite chased a fortnight early is usually still cheap to move.
DEP_AT_RISK.title: Dependency at risk
DEP_AT_RISK.message: {sourceName} waits on {targetName}, which someone has flagged at risk.
DEP_AT_RISK.explanation: Status was set to at risk by a person, not derived.
DEP_AT_RISK.why: Someone already knows this is in trouble. The signal makes sure that knowledge is not stuck with them.
DEP_NO_NEEDED_BY.title: Prerequisite with no date
DEP_NO_NEEDED_BY.message: {sourceName} needs {targetName}, but no date is set.
DEP_NO_NEEDED_BY.explanation: This is a hard dependency, so the work cannot proceed without it.
DEP_NO_NEEDED_BY.why: A prerequisite with no date cannot be chased, and cannot be shown to be late.
DEP_TARGET_MOVED_LATE.title: Prerequisite now lands too late
DEP_TARGET_MOVED_LATE.message: {targetName} is targeted at {targetQuarter}; {sourceName} needs it by {sourceQuarter}.
DEP_TARGET_MOVED_LATE.explanation: The thing being waited on now finishes no earlier than the thing waiting.
DEP_TARGET_MOVED_LATE.why: The dependency is unsatisfiable as planned. One of the two targets has to move.
DEP_TARGET_AFTER_NEEDED_BY.title: Prerequisite dated after it is needed
DEP_TARGET_AFTER_NEEDED_BY.message: {targetName} is due {targetDate}, {daysLate} days after the {neededBy} it is needed by.
DEP_TARGET_AFTER_NEEDED_BY.why: The dates already disagree. Better to resolve that now than at the point it blocks delivery.
DEP_CYCLE.title: Circular dependency
DEP_CYCLE.explanation: Each piece of work in the cycle waits on another piece in the same cycle.
DEP_CYCLE.why: Cycles are allowed — sometimes two things genuinely need each other — but none of them can start without a decision about sequencing.
DEP_HUB.title: Bottleneck
DEP_HUB.message: {targetName} has {incoming} unresolved things waiting on it.
DEP_HUB.explanation: Every one of those is blocked by the same target.
DEP_HUB.why: A single bottleneck is where the most delay can be removed for the least effort.
DEP_HUB_CONSTRAINED.title: Bottleneck with no capacity
DEP_HUB_CONSTRAINED.message: {targetName} has {incoming} things waiting on it and is over capacity in {quarterId}.
DEP_HUB_CONSTRAINED.explanation: The team many pieces of work depend on has no room to do them.
DEP_HUB_CONSTRAINED.why: This is usually the single most useful thing on a portfolio radar: everything queued behind a team that cannot move.
DEP_DECISION_OVERDUE.title: Decision overdue
DEP_DECISION_OVERDUE.why: Work waiting on a decision is work nobody is doing, and nobody is accountable for the wait.
DEP_DECISION_UNOWNED.title: Decision has no owner
DEP_DECISION_UNOWNED.message: {decision} is needed by {neededBy} and nobody owns it.
DEP_DECISION_UNOWNED.explanation: A decision with a date and no owner has nobody to make it.
DEP_DECISION_UNOWNED.why: Dates do not chase themselves. Someone has to be asked.
DEP_TARGET_ARCHIVED.title: Dependency points at archived work
DEP_TARGET_ARCHIVED.message: {sourceName} waits on {targetName}, which has been archived.
DEP_TARGET_ARCHIVED.explanation: The target is no longer active, so the dependency can never resolve.
DEP_TARGET_ARCHIVED.why: A dependency on something that no longer exists will sit open forever and quietly distort every count.
DEP_BLOCKED_IN_DELIVERY.title: In delivery and blocked
DEP_BLOCKED_IN_DELIVERY.message: {sourceName} is in delivery, blocked by {targetName} since {neededBy}.
DEP_BLOCKED_IN_DELIVERY.explanation: A hard prerequisite has been overdue for {daysOverdue} days.
DEP_BLOCKED_IN_DELIVERY.why: Work in delivery that is blocked is burning capacity without producing anything.
ATT_DATE_REACHED.title: Attention date reached
ATT_DATE_REACHED.explanation: Someone set this date deliberately to be reminded.
ATT_DATE_REACHED.why: The date is a note from your past self. It is worth reading before it is a surprise.
ACT_OVERDUE.title: Next action overdue
ACT_OVERDUE.explanation: The next action has a date, and the date has passed.
ACT_OVERDUE.why: The next action is the smallest unit of progress the product tracks. When it stalls, everything behind it does.
ACT_DUE_SOON.title: Next action due soon
ACT_DUE_SOON.explanation: The next action falls inside the reminder window.
ACT_DUE_SOON.why: Small enough to do now, expensive to forget.
ACT_MISSING.title: No next action
ACT_MISSING.message: {commitment} is in delivery with no next action, last updated {lastUpdated}.
ACT_MISSING.explanation: Nothing has changed on it for {days} days.
ACT_MISSING.why: Work in delivery with no stated next step is usually work nobody has picked up.
TGT_MISSED.title: Target date missed
TGT_MISSED.explanation: The lifecycle is still {lifecycle}, so the work is not finished.
TGT_MISSED.why: A target that has passed without a decision is a commitment the organisation still believes in and is not getting.
TGT_APPROACHING.title: Target approaching
TGT_APPROACHING.explanation: The target date falls inside the reminder window.
TGT_APPROACHING.why: Late enough to be real, early enough to change something.
TGT_QUARTER_OVERRUN.title: Placed later than its target
TGT_QUARTER_OVERRUN.message: {commitment} targets {targetQuarterId} but has work placed in {latestQuarterId}.
TGT_QUARTER_OVERRUN.explanation: The placement and the target disagree.
TGT_QUARTER_OVERRUN.why: One of the two is wrong, and whichever it is, someone is planning against the other.
LSS_PASSED.title: Latest safe start passed
LSS_PASSED.message: {commitment} had to start by {latestSafeStart}, {daysOverdue} days ago.
LSS_PASSED.explanation: It is still {lifecycle}, so it has not started.
LSS_PASSED.why: The latest safe start is the last day the target was reachable. It no longer is.
LSS_APPROACHING.title: Latest safe start approaching
LSS_APPROACHING.why: After this date the target stops being achievable, whatever anyone commits to.
MS_OVERDUE.title: Milestone overdue
MS_OVERDUE.explanation: The milestone is still marked planned.
MS_OVERDUE.why: A milestone that quietly slips is how a target date is missed without anyone noticing until the end.
MS_DUE_SOON.title: Milestone due soon
MS_DUE_SOON.explanation: The milestone is still marked planned.
MS_DUE_SOON.why: Checkable points are the cheapest early warning a plan has.
MS_MISSED_FLAGGED.title: Milestone marked missed
MS_MISSED_FLAGGED.explanation: Missed is set by a person, never derived from a date.
MS_MISSED_FLAGGED.why: Someone made a judgement that this point was not reached. The plan behind it probably needs revisiting.
RDY_NO_PRIMARY_TEAM.title: No team owns this yet
RDY_NO_PRIMARY_TEAM.message: {commitment} has capacity placed but no primary team.
RDY_NO_PRIMARY_TEAM.explanation: The Commit Gate needs one team accountable for the work.
RDY_NO_PRIMARY_TEAM.why: Work that several teams touch and none owns is work that stalls at the first disagreement.
RDY_NO_FOOTPRINT.title: Targeted but not placed
RDY_NO_FOOTPRINT.explanation: The idea has a quarter in mind but no capacity behind it.
RDY_NO_FOOTPRINT.why: A target quarter without a placement is a wish, not a plan.
RDY_NO_OUTCOME.title: No outcome stated
RDY_NO_OUTCOME.explanation: Nothing records what will be true once this is done.
RDY_NO_OUTCOME.why: Without a stated outcome there is no way to tell later whether it worked.
RDY_NO_PRODUCT_IMPACT.title: No product impact recorded
RDY_NO_PRODUCT_IMPACT.message: {commitment} does not say which product or service it changes.
RDY_NO_PRODUCT_IMPACT.why: Change load is measured per product. Work that names no product is change nobody can see coming.
RDY_NO_DEPENDENCIES_REVIEWED.title: Dependencies not reviewed
RDY_NO_DEPENDENCIES_REVIEWED.message: Nobody has recorded whether {commitment} depends on anything.
RDY_NO_DEPENDENCIES_REVIEWED.explanation: Zero dependencies may be correct — but it has not been said.
RDY_NO_DEPENDENCIES_REVIEWED.why: The commonest cause of a surprise dependency is that nobody was ever asked the question.
RDY_LOW_CONFIDENCE_LARGE.title: Large, and sized with low confidence
RDY_LOW_CONFIDENCE_LARGE.message: {commitment} is {units} units with low size confidence.
RDY_LOW_CONFIDENCE_LARGE.explanation: Work this large is being planned on a number the team is unsure of.
RDY_LOW_CONFIDENCE_LARGE.why: A big number nobody trusts will move, and everything placed after it moves too.
RDY_IDEA_UNREFINED.title: Idea sitting untouched
RDY_IDEA_UNREFINED.message: {commitment} was captured {createdOn}, {days} days ago, and has had no refinement.
RDY_IDEA_UNREFINED.explanation: It has no refinement-reserve link and no placement.
RDY_IDEA_UNREFINED.why: Ideas that are never refined are not a backlog — they are a list nobody reads.
RDY_MANDATORY_NO_TARGET.title: Mandatory work with no date
RDY_MANDATORY_NO_TARGET.message: {commitment} is mandatory and has no target date.
RDY_MANDATORY_NO_TARGET.why: Mandatory work has a deadline whether or not it is recorded. Recording it is the only way to plan around it.
OWN_MISSING.title: No owner
OWN_MISSING.why: Ownership is asked for at commitment rather than at capture, precisely so this signal means something.
OWN_TEAM_ONLY_ACTION_DUE.title: Action due, owned by a team
OWN_TEAM_ONLY_ACTION_DUE.message: {commitment} has an action due {nextActionDueDate} owned by a team, not a person.
OWN_TEAM_ONLY_ACTION_DUE.explanation: A team owns the next action, due in {daysUntil} days.
OWN_TEAM_ONLY_ACTION_DUE.why: A team cannot be chased. A person can.
OWN_DEPENDENCY_MISSING.title: Dependency has no owner
OWN_DEPENDENCY_MISSING.message: A {type} dependency is needed by {neededBy} and nobody owns it.
OWN_DEPENDENCY_MISSING.explanation: Nobody has been asked to resolve it.
OWN_DEPENDENCY_MISSING.why: Dependencies do not resolve themselves; somebody has to go and ask.
OWN_ARCHIVED.title: Owner no longer here
OWN_ARCHIVED.message: {commitment} is owned by {person}, who has been archived.
OWN_ARCHIVED.explanation: The owner record is no longer active.
OWN_ARCHIVED.why: Work owned by someone who has left is work that is effectively unowned.
HLT_STALE_DELIVERY.title: In delivery, not updated
HLT_STALE_DELIVERY.message: {commitment} has not changed for {days} days, since {lastUpdated}.
HLT_STALE_DELIVERY.explanation: It is in delivery, so something should be moving.
HLT_STALE_DELIVERY.why: Silence on work in delivery usually means it has stopped, and nobody has said so.
HLT_STALE_COMMITTED.title: Committed, not reviewed
HLT_STALE_COMMITTED.message: {commitment} has not changed for {days} days, since {lastUpdated}.
HLT_STALE_COMMITTED.explanation: It is committed but has not been touched.
HLT_STALE_COMMITTED.why: A commitment nobody has looked at in months is a commitment nobody is really making.
HLT_STALE_HELD.title: Held for a long time
HLT_STALE_HELD.message: {commitment} has been on hold for {days} days, still holding {units} units.
HLT_STALE_HELD.explanation: The capacity was preserved when it was held.
HLT_STALE_HELD.why: Held work that keeps its capacity blocks a quarter without delivering anything. Either resume it or release the room.
HLT_MOVED_REPEATEDLY.title: Target keeps moving
HLT_MOVED_REPEATEDLY.message: {commitment} has moved to a later quarter {moves} times.
HLT_MOVED_REPEATEDLY.why: Work that keeps slipping is rarely fixed by slipping again. The estimate or the scope is usually the problem.
HLT_GROWN.title: Grown since commitment
HLT_GROWN.message: {commitment} is now {units} units, up from {unitsAtCommit} at the gate — {percent}% larger.
HLT_GROWN.explanation: The size recorded at the Commit Gate was {unitsAtCommit}.
HLT_GROWN.why: Growth after commitment is the quiet way a quarter fills up. Whoever agreed to the original number should know.
PRD_CHANGE_LOAD_HIGH.title: High change load
PRD_CHANGE_LOAD_HIGH.message: {product} carries a change load of {score} in {quarterId}, above the {threshold} threshold.
PRD_CHANGE_LOAD_HIGH.explanation: {contributors} pieces of work land on it, the largest being {topContributor}.
PRD_CHANGE_LOAD_HIGH.why: A product absorbing a lot of change at once is where incidents come from, however well each individual change is run.
PRD_CONCENTRATION.title: Change concentrated on one product
PRD_CONCENTRATION.explanation: Each is a primary or major impact.
PRD_CONCENTRATION.why: The map shows who does the work; it cannot show that five teams are all changing the same thing.
PRD_MANDATORY_STACK.title: Mandatory work stacked on one product
PRD_MANDATORY_STACK.why: When several immovable changes land on one product in one quarter, the only remaining lever is sequencing — and it has to be pulled early.
PRD_NO_OWNER.title: Product has no owner
PRD_NO_OWNER.message: {product} has a {level} change load in {quarterId} and no owner.
PRD_NO_OWNER.explanation: Nobody is recorded as accountable for the product.
PRD_NO_OWNER.why: Somebody has to be able to say whether the product can absorb what is coming.
INT_DANGLING_REF.title: Reference to missing data
INT_DANGLING_REF.message: {fromRef} points at {toRef}, which does not exist.
INT_DANGLING_REF.explanation: The target was removed without the reference being cleaned up.
INT_DANGLING_REF.why: Dangling references distort counts and can hide work entirely. They are always a defect, never a plan.
INT_SCHEMA_AHEAD.title: Data from a newer version
INT_SCHEMA_AHEAD.message: {entityRef} was written by schema version {schemaVersion}; this build understands {buildSchemaVersion}.
INT_SCHEMA_AHEAD.explanation: The row came from a newer build of Flowmap.
INT_SCHEMA_AHEAD.why: Reported rather than ignored: a build that silently drops what it does not understand loses somebody’s work.
SEC_SECRET_SUSPECTED.title: Possible credential in a note
SEC_SECRET_SUSPECTED.message: Something shaped like a credential ({patternId}) appears in {field}: {preview}.
SEC_SECRET_SUSPECTED.explanation: The pattern is matched exactly; the matched text is never stored or sent anywhere.
SEC_SECRET_SUSPECTED.why: Notes are exported, synchronised, and read by people who should not have your keys.
